bullets.text: Mobilized catastrophe plan for Hurricane Ian; retained $200M of $1.4B direct Property losses; special lines Ian losses estimated at $290M; distributed supplies from Fort Myers; over 1,000 employees picked up extra hours.
Q3 CR was 99.2 (YTD 96.5) with 7.1 pts of cat losses; personal lines CR was 100; Commercial Lines CR reached 89.7; Property CR was 125.1, reflecting 36 pts of retained Ian losses.
Companywide NPW +5% to bring YTD growth to 8%; Personal Lines NPW +9%; Commercial Lines NPW -13% due to TNC renewal timing (+2% adjusted); Property NPW +3%.

Rate increases in 20 states averaged ~2% countrywide in Q3, bringing YTD increases to nearly 12%; earning-in of prior rate increases helped non-catastrophe personal auto achieve target profit margins.
Total auto PIF fell 1% YOY but increased nearly 250,000 from June 2022; personal auto PIF was 17.4M; Commercial Lines PIF grew 9%; Property PIF grew 4%; quoting rose over 20%.

Underlying average loss costs continued rising due to higher severity from general economic inflation, while calendar-year frequency remained more stable quarter to quarter and operated below pre-pandemic levels.

Competitor rate increases improved Progressive's competitive positioning, which management believes is evidenced in 20% total auto new business application growth; quoting increased more than 20% in both channels.

Total portfolio return was -1.9% (fixed income -1.8%, equity -4.5%) as monetary policy remained aggressive; Progressive maintains a conservative investment posture and expects current uncertainty to eventually lead to interesting opportunities.

Personal auto model 8.8 reached six states (11% of premium); commercial auto policy administration system reached 33 states; BOP expanded to 37 states, with nearly 70% of policies sold without underwriting review.

Over 200 CRM employees signed up to work in different workgroups during Hurricane Ian; leaders and coworkers rallied to provide housing, furniture, clothing, and financial assistance to an impacted colleague.
